Acids and bases are measured on the PH scale, neutral is 7, acids are below and bases are above. It’s a logarithmic Scale so each whole point away from 7 is 10 Times the previous point.

Some canned sauces from cheap unripe tomato’s are wickedly acidic and will cause an unbalanced set of flavors on the palette and even upset the stomach of some.

Try this instead the next batch of sauce for say a pasta.

Make sauce as usual, then remove a cup of it aside, add 1/16 tsp ( or a tiny pinch)of baking soda and stir in for a minute. Taste side by side with pot of sauce. Repeat. Repeat... at some point, when you just pass neutral the sauce goes slightly brown from red and takes on the distinct note of chef Boyardee. Ick. A few doses back is usually the best balance, sometimes more or less depending on the meal.

If you have a fancy PH meter (or even test strips) you can dial in your preference for sauce by PH number and hit it every time.

Let me know how it goes the next time you make sauce. (This tip is mostly for canned tomato sauce, or fresh tomato sauce, or canned diced tomatoes. Pre made pasta sauce is already somewhat balanced.)
